scenes.title: Opening image
scenes.narration: Why won't this drive eject? Meet PhantomTrace.

scenes.title: The problem
scenes.narration: You try to eject a drive from Finder. It says a program may be using it. It never says which one. You can only try again, or force it.
scenes.record: Optional live clip. In Finder, select PhantomDemo, press Cmd+E. Let the dialog sit for 3 seconds.

scenes.title: The old way

lines.text: Volume PhantomDemo on disk8s1 failed to unmount: dissented by PID 95849 (/usr/bin/tail)
COMMAND   PID    USER   FD   TYPE DEVICE SIZE/OFF NODE NAME

scenes.narration: Today that means lsof, guesswork, and sometimes pulling the cable. Even diskutil names only one process.
scenes.record: Optional live clip instead of the replay: run both commands in Terminal against the demo drive.

scenes.title: The trigger
scenes.narration: PhantomTrace starts where you are stuck. Right-click the drive, choose Why Can't I Eject, and the ghost appears.
scenes.record: REQUIRED. Finder, right-click PhantomDemo on the Desktop or sidebar, Quick Actions, Why Can't I Eject? Stop when the PhantomTrace window opens. About 10 seconds.

scenes.title: The reveal
scenes.narration: Press Summon the Phantom Trace. The list names every process: an idle zsh sitting in the volume, and a tail holding a file open. You see the name, the process I D, and the file.
scenes.record: Optional live clip. Let the window open, then slowly move the pointer over each row.

scenes.title: Where the look comes from
scenes.narration: A note on the look. It carries over from my 2025 Kiroween entry, West of House, a spooky retelling of the classic text game Zork. That dark woodcut style now lives in a System 7 and Mac O S 9 platinum window, with its status icons and outline. The art was made fresh for this project.

callouts.text: Style carried over from West of House (2025)

scenes.record: No recording needed. Optional: show a West of House screenshot beside this window, but only if you own it and add it to docs/Assets.md first.

scenes.title: Safety first
scenes.narration: Nothing runs until you choose it. Each stage shows a plan first, and says why any process was skipped. Protected processes and other users' processes are never touched.
scenes.record: Optional live clip. Choose a stage and press Proceed; stop on the plan preview.

scenes.title: Stage 1: Egress Shells
scenes.narration: Stage one, Egress Shells. The idle shell goes home. The prompt changes. The shell is not killed.
scenes.record: REQUIRED. Show the demo Terminal window and the PhantomTrace window side by side. Choose Egress Shells, Proceed, confirm. The Terminal prompt should change to ~. Keep going until the lock list updates. About 15 seconds.

scenes.title: Stage 2: Graceful Request
scenes.narration: Stage two, Graceful Request. PhantomTrace asks the program to quit, waits, and scans again. Anything still holding the drive stays on the list.
scenes.record: Optional live clip. Choose Graceful Request, Proceed, confirm, then let the rescan finish.

scenes.title: Stage 3: Banish Locks
scenes.narration: Stage three is a last resort. It names each process and its I D, and waits for your confirmation. Here, it is not needed.
scenes.record: Optional live clip. Only needed if a lock is still left after stage two.

scenes.title: Clean Handoff
scenes.narration: When a fresh scan finds zero locks, the haunting is over. Eject unmounts the volume the normal way, and the drive icon is gone.

callouts.text: Zero locks, then a normal unmount

scenes.record: REQUIRED. From the clear state press Eject. Show the green VOLUME RELEASED window and the drive leaving Finder. About 10 seconds. The still shows if there is no clip.

scenes.title: Built with Kiro
scenes.narration: Kiro shaped this build. Specs defined the safety rules, steering kept the code consistent, and hooks check lint, tests, and the project log before commits.
scenes.record: Optional live clip: Kiro showing .kiro/specs, steering and hooks, then a passing swift test run.

scenes.title: Close

titleCard.headline: PhantomTrace
titleCard.sub: Resurrecting "What's Keeping Me?" for modern macOS

scenes.narration: PhantomTrace resurrects the classic What's Keeping Me idea for modern macOS. Local only, no network, nothing hidden.
